title: Streptavidin Yielding with Ponceau Stain
author: Manuela De Las Casas
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6euhbew

steps.title: Create Wax Circle on Nitrocellulose
steps.instruction: Create a wax boundary on a nitrocellulose strip using a hot plate and a pipette tip.

substeps.instruction: Set the hot plate to 100ºC or a temperature sufficient to melt wax.
Place a small amount of wax from a wax pencil onto a Petri dish on the hot plate and wait for it to melt.
Cut a nitrocellulose sheet strip to the desired size.
Dip the broad end of a 200μL pipette tip into the melted wax.
Press the tip onto the nitrocellulose strip to create a wax circle and remove the tip.
Sandwich the strip between two sheets of paper.
Place the sandwich on the hot plate with a Petri dish (or any temperature-resistant flat object) on top to apply pressure.
Warm for 5 minutes to allow wax penetration.
Remove and let the strip cool, ensuring the center of the circle remains clear.

steps.title: Apply Streptavidin
steps.instruction: Apply the protein to the center of the wax circle and dry.

substeps.instruction: Pipette 5 μL of Streptavidin (e.g., suspended in PBS without dilutions) into the center of the wax circle.
Allow the protein to dry completely at room temperature.

steps.title: Stain and Wash Strip
steps.instruction: Stain the strip with Ponceau stain to visualize the protein.

substeps.instruction: Place the strip in a Petri dish and soak it completely in Ponceau stain.
Wash the strip repeatedly with water until the edges (areas without protein) are clear.
